I'm identifying the center block and calculating the direction from it to each surrounding object, then determining which way to shoot from each object's own center based on that relative position.

Working through the coordinates, I find the projected trails: from (3,5) extending diagonally up-right to (0,8), from (6,2) extending down-right to (8,0), and from (6,5) extending down-right to (9,8), filling out the final grid pattern.

content.text:
I'm identifying the block as a 4-cell object centered at (6,3), with satellite cells at (4,1), (4,4), and (7,4) treated as separate single-cell objects since they aren't orthogonally connected to it. Now I'm working out the relative position of each satellite to the block's center.

For (4,1), the block is below-right, so I shoot a diagonal ray from the satellite up-left, giving cells (4,1) and (3,0). For (4,4), the block is below-left, so the ray goes up-right: (3,5),(2,6),(1,7),(0,8). For (7,4), the block is above-left, so the ray goes down-right: (7,4),(8,5),(9,6). Now I need to assemble these into the output grid.
